passages.text: Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.
passages.note: Division within a family, group or oneself

passages.text: For out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks. The good man out of his good treasure brings out good things, and the evil man out of his evil treasure brings out evil things.
passages.note: Words reveal the heart; speech and character

passages.text: Behold, a farmer went out to sow. As he sowed, some seeds fell by the roadside, and the birds came and devoured them. Others fell on rocky ground, where they didn’t have much soil, and immediately they sprang up, because they had no depth of earth. When the sun had risen, they were scorched. Because they had no root, they withered away. Others fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked them. Others fell on good soil, and yielded fruit: some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.
passages.note: Efforts that fail and efforts that flourish; receptivity

passages.text: The Kingdom of Heaven is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field; which indeed is smaller than all seeds. But when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs, and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches.
passages.note: Small beginnings growing into something great

passages.text: A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and in his own house.
passages.note: Not being valued by family or hometown
